records.quote: The objectives of SAFFIRE-II are to determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity and to investigate the low-g flammability limits compared to those obtained in NASA’s normal gravity material flammability screening test.
records.derivation: Objective statement, not a statement of the conditions of the completed tests; 'low-gravity' mapped to the controlled value microgravity. The 'normal gravity' screening test named here is NASA's ground test, not a test of this investigation.

records.quote: The specific objective of SAFFIRE-II tests is to quantify that affect in long-duration low-gravity using samples of the same size as those used in the NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 normal-gravity tests.
records.derivation: Objective statement specific to SAFFIRE-II; 'long-duration low-gravity' mapped to microgravity. The 'NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 normal-gravity tests' are the ground reference, not tests reported in PSI-99.

records.quote: Results determine microgravity flammability limits for several spacecraft materials, help to validate NASA’s material selection criteria, and how microgravity and limited oxygen affect flame size.
records.derivation: Research-impact statement about the results; it does not say explicitly that the tests were conducted in microgravity.

records.source_file: psi-data/PSI-99/Science Documents/PSI-99_Science Documents_SAFFIRE Objectives, Development and Status.pdf
records.quote: This paper describes the three Spacecraft Fire Experiments (Saffire-I, -II, and -III) that were developed at NASA-GRC and that will conduct a series of material flammability tests in low-gravity and at length scales that are realistic for a spacecraft fire.
records.derivation: Pre-flight paper (future tense, launches 'all planned for 2016'); the sentence covers Saffire-I, -II and -III together; 'low-gravity' mapped to microgravity.

records.value_original: SIBAL, silicone, structure PMMA, flat PMMA, and PMMA with Nomex
records.quote: As a follow on to the Saffire-I investigation, the Saffire-II investigation added more samples including SIBAL, silicone, structure PMMA, flat PMMA, and PMMA with Nomex.
records.derivation: Inferred from the material names (SIBAL cloth, silicone, PMMA, Nomex are solid materials); the sentence does not name the phase.

records.quote: The Saffire-II experiment was performed on the Orbital Science’s Cygnus resupply vehicle after it deberthed from the ISS.

records.source_file: psi-data/PSI-99/Science Documents/PSI-99_Science Documents_SAFFIRE Objectives, Development and Status.pdf
records.quote: The experiments will be conducted in Orbital ATK’s Cygnus vehicle after it has unberthed from the International Space Station.
records.derivation: Pre-flight, future tense; the sentence covers Saffire-I, -II and -III together. It names the operator as Orbital ATK where the PSI record (R6) says Orbital Science’s; both name the Cygnus vehicle.

records.quote: Depending on the sample material, the Saffire-II was conducted at an air flow velocity of either 20 or 30 cm/s, the flow being either concurrent or opposed.
records.derivation: air: oxygen balanced mainly by nitrogen. None of the three sources names the balance gas of the Cygnus atmosphere.

records.quote: Flame spread over a large thin charring surface in low-gravity showed that steady flame spread was possible (unlike normal gravity)
records.derivation: derived: source says 'low-gravity' (orbital free flight in Cygnus). Results slide titled 'Saffire-I-III Results' of Urban et al., ASGSR 2017 (NTRS 20180005168): it covers the three flights together, so it is not independent per flight.

not_found.looked_in: Record text, all sections (approach: 'solid state sensors were used to measure pressure'; researchImpacts: instruments 'measure ... pressure'; no value or range). SAFFIRE-II Readme paragraphs 1-83 (no pressure; Tables 1 and 3 appear in the dump only as captions, paragraphs 3 and 52). Objectives PDF pages 1-6 (page 3, Table 2 lists 'Pressure solid-state sensor in avionics bay', no value). The experimental table CSV and the Image Directory Nomenclature PDF were not among the assigned sources.

Partial: record text, Readme paragraphs 1-83 and PDF pages 1-6 contain no sentence stating as fact that the SAFFIRE-II burns took place in microgravity/low gravity; only objectives (R1, R2), an impact statement (R3) and a pre-flight plan (R4), all ambiguous. No normal-gravity (1-g) tests are reported in PSI-99: the 'NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 normal-gravity tests' (Readme paragraph 1) and the 'normal gravity Maximum Oxygen Concentration (MOC) flammability limits' (PDF page 2) are existing ground screening data cited for comparison, with no test ids, so no normal_gravity record was proposed.

lineage: The Objectives PDF (NTRS 20170001636 per its page-1 header) is also filed as PSI-98 and PSI-100 'SAFFIRE Objectives, Development and Status.pdf' and covers Saffire-I, -II and -III jointly: 'The premise for the design of the flight experiment was that practically all of the hardware would be identical in the three units except possibly for the sample material(s) to be burned.' (page=2); its Table 2 is titled 'Saffire-I, II, and III Diagnostics' (page=3), and the record approach calls Saffire-II 'a follow on to the Saffire-I investigation'. SIBAL fabric (Saffire-II samples S5 and S6, PDF page=3 Table 1) comes from an earlier flight experiment: 'It is called SIBAL cloth because it was developed for the Solid Inflammability Boundary at Low-Speeds (SIBAL) spaceflight experiment [...]' (page=2, in the paragraph on Saffire-I and III material). The Readme paragraph=1 objective sentences repeat the PDF abstract and page-3 wording. The ISS appears only as the station Cygnus left before the test; it is not the test platform.
